transit.name: FLEX
transit.detail: Regional bus operated by Transfort with stops between Fort Collins, Loveland, Berthoud, Longmont and Boulder

nameOrigin.text: David Barnes named the town for William A. H. Loveland, president of the Colorado Central Railroad.

founded.text: Laid out by farmer David Barnes as a station town on the Colorado Central Railroad

timeline.text: In September, farmer David Barnes laid out a townsite on his wheat field north of the Big Thompson River.
Loveland was incorporated, a year after the 1880 census counted 256 residents.
Harold Dunning founded the museum that became the Loveland Museum.
The City of Loveland took over operation of Dunning's pioneer museum.
The Downtown Loveland Historic District was listed on the National Register on June 1.

sites.name: Loveland Museum
sites.hours: Tuesday–Wednesday 11 am–5 pm; Thursday–Friday 11 am–7 pm; Saturday 10 am–4 pm; closed Sunday and Monday
sites.cost: $7 Loveland residents; $10 non-residents; free 12 and under

sites.name: Benson Sculpture Garden
sites.hours: Open at any time of day
sites.cost: Free, except during the Sculpture in the Park show weekend, the second weekend in August
sites.season: Year-round; a small section closes during show setup and takedown

trails.name: Devil’s Backbone Open Space
trails.size: 3,007 acres along the sandstone hogback west of Loveland, with 17.25 miles of shared trail that connect north through Rimrock to Horsetooth Mountain
trails.trailhead: Off U.S. 34 just past mile marker 88, 2 miles west of the Jax store: north on Hidden Valley Drive, just east of the old water tank; the lot is on the left, with restrooms and water
trails.season: Day use, sunrise to sunset; the gate typically opens by 6 am. The lot fills on weekends and holidays, and the County says to come before 10 am or after 4 pm.
trails.dogs: On a leash at all times; the County asks that they stay home in hot weather.
trails.fee: A Larimer County entrance permit is required.

trails.name: Boyd Lake State Park
trails.size: A 1,700-acre lake when full, with 361 acres of land, 140 paved campsites and more than 200 bird species
trails.address: 3720 N. County Road 11-C, Loveland, the park’s only entrance
trails.season: Open daily, 5 am to 10 pm. Low water has closed the lake to boating for the rest of 2026; kayaks, paddleboards and swimming are still allowed. The marina is closed for the 2026 season.
trails.dogs: On a leash and under control at all times.
trails.fee: A daily vehicle pass, $10 to $12 with Colorado plates or $15 to $17 out of state; when the entrance gate is unattended, buy it at the self-service kiosk.

trails.name: Chapungu Sculpture Park at Centerra
trails.size: 26 acres of natural and landscaped gardens and trails, with 82 monumental stone sculptures by Zimbabwean artists
trails.address: Just east of the Promenade Shops at Centerra, off U.S. 34 and Centerra Parkway, Loveland
trails.season: Open every day of the year, 6 am to 10 pm. The public restroom opens during summer hours.
trails.dogs: Dog-friendly, with a pet water fountain.
